title: ICE Field Offices Get, Then Lose, Verbal Order to Stop Arresting Immigrants Without Criminal Records
detail: ICE officers nationwide received verbal guidance over the weekend of Saturday, September 26, 2026 — first reported by The Daily Wire's Jennie Taer — instructing them to arrest only undocumented immigrants with criminal convictions or pending charges 'for the time being,' effectively ending so-called 'collateral arrests' of bystanders encountered during operations targeting someone else. Agents described being 'shocked and frustrated' by the order, according to Fox News correspondent Bill Melugin, who said none of the nine ICE and DHS sources he spoke with could identify who originated it. New guidance reversing the order went out to field offices Saturday evening, with officials characterizing the episode as a 'miscommunication' during internal conversations about prioritizing 'worst first' rather than an actual policy change. DHS posted on X: 'This is false. No one is off the table. We will continue to arrest any and all illegal aliens that come into our path.' President Trump told Fox News that ICE 'can still arrest and deport anyone who is in the country illegally,' confirming arrests of non-criminal immigrants, including collaterals, would continue.

title: Austin City Council Candidate Misael Ramos Arrested on Riot Charge Over Protest of ICE Shooting
detail: Misael Ramos, a democratic-socialist candidate for Austin City Council, was arrested by Texas Department of Public Safety troopers around 8:50 a.m. on Saturday, September 26, 2026, near Stafford Street and Manor Road while walking his dog, on a Class B misdemeanor charge of riot participation. DPS said a warrant was issued after Ramos was allegedly seen on camera moving construction barricades, sandbags, and other items to obstruct traffic during a September 20, 2026 demonstration that followed the ICE shooting of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan DoorDash driver, in North Austin. Ramos was booked at the Travis County Jail and released on $1,000 bail Saturday afternoon. His attorney, Edmund 'Skip' Davis, disputed the 'riot' characterization, saying he saw 'people chanting and protesting rather than rioting,' and Ramos's campaign said he intends to contest the charge.
